Function definitions (pkgver, build, package) are out of scope for this gate. All variable assignments are routine packaging metadata. There is no obfuscated code, encoding, or data exfiltration at the sourcing stage.

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is the standard AUR `.SRCINFO` metadata file for the `shelltrace-git` package. It contains only packaging metadata: package name, description, version string, URLs, architecture, license, build/runtime dependencies, and the source declaration. There is no executable code, no shell logic, no encoding/obfuscation, and no commands of any kind.

The `source` points to the project's own upstream repository (`git+https://github.com/hamdyaea/ShellTrace.git`), which is the expected origin for this package. The `sha256sums = SKIP` value is the normal and required practice for VCS (`git+`) sources, not a red flag. Dependencies (`qt6-base`, `strace`, `bubblewrap`) and makedepends (`git`, `rust`, `cmake`, `gcc`) are all consistent with a Rust CLI + Qt6 GUI application. No suspicious network destinations, data exfiltration, backdoors, or system tampering are present.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard AUR metadata; source points to own upstream, no threats.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard AUR packaging script for shelltrace-git, a Rust CLI and Qt6 GUI tool. It fetches source only from the declared upstream GitHub repository (git+https://github.com/hamdyaea/ShellTrace.git), uses SKIP checksums (normal for VCS sources), builds with cargo and cmake, and installs binaries, a desktop file, an icon, and documentation into $pkgdir. No obfuscated code, no network exfiltration, no eval/base64/curl patterns, and no modification of unrelated system files are present. The build() function defensively pins PATH to /usr/bin to avoid user-level rustup shims, which is routine packaging hygiene, not malicious behavior.
</details>
